creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`input.key` records only keys that reach a pane. A chord the keymap consumes is logged by its effect, when the effect has a line of its own, and never by the press. So a run log cannot tell someone holding `cmd+-` from Muster resizing a pane on its own.

## What was measured

Run 34598, 2026-09-04: 16,589 `input.key` lines, 2 with `super` in `mods`, on a day spent switching panes and tabs with cmd chords. `input.bound.text` exists for the `[text]` table (165 lines, `pane_input.rs:123`); there is no sibling for actions. `pane_input.rs:177` logs a key after the bindings have had their turn.

What it cost: eight `pane.font_size` lines 100 ms apart, each followed by a `bridge.resize` 30 ms later, growing a pane from 349x95 to 931x248 (`a_2KHGYMpnK`). That is exactly what a replay bug looks like, and it was called one in this session until the doc comment on `adjust_font_size` ("one press of a font-size chord") settled it. The log had every effect and none of the causes.

## Fix

Log the press where the binding resolves: `input.bound.action` beside `input.bound.text`, with key, mods, the action's name from `Action::ALL`, and whether the event was a repeat. Debug level, like `input.key`. A chord can also arrive as a menu item's key equivalent (`MenuActions.swift:143`); both paths run the same action and should write the same record, with a `source` field, so a reader need not know which one fired.
title: 🔎 A bound chord leaves no trace in the run log, so a held key and a bug look the same
